interpretation: Candidate steady-state explicit submission avoids repeated heuristic enumeration and descriptor validation while preserving the observed submitted algorithm and launch configuration.

All28 native submissions share the exact64-byte descriptor and all7 queried public attributes; all40 traced kernel launches share name,grid,block,register,shared-memory and recorded occupancy metadata.
The default-normalized graph ratio is neutral for these three trials; raw graph differences co-move with the default control.
Candidate explicit remains slightly slower than its own default in eager timing; removing the old explicit-path enumeration cost does not establish a better winner or full serving benefit.
These are observed launch signatures; the audit does not claim instruction-level identity or isolate every remaining CPU setup component.
